commits.author: Prahlad Gowtham <prahladgowtham@gmail.com>
commits.message:
Makefile: fix universal build when source directory path contains spaces

GNU Make uses unescaped whitespace as separators in target and prerequisite lists. In Section 6 (Universal binary driver), defining `TEMP_DIR`, `UNIVERSAL_EXE`, and `UNIVERSAL_SRC_DIR` using `$(CURDIR)` causes Make to split paths containing spaces into multiple nonexistent targets. This produces recipe override warnings, circular dependency warnings, and missing target errors during universal builds (as reported in #7259).

### Changes
- Use relative paths for `TEMP_DIR` (`temp_builds`), `UNIVERSAL_EXE` (`$(EXE)`), and `UNIVERSAL_SRC_DIR` (`universal`).
- Wrap the standard single-arch `$(EXE): $(OBJS)` rule with `ifeq ($(UNIVERSAL_BUILD),false)` to avoid duplicate rule warnings against `$(UNIVERSAL_EXE)`.
- Pass relative `NNUE_EMBED_OBJ=../nnue_embed.o` to per-arch sub-make invocations.
- Use relative symlinks `ln -s ../../$(f)` in the `.setup` rule.
- Use relative `--embed-dir=.` and `--embed-dir=../..` rather than absolute paths.
- Quote shell command paths in recipes (`cd "$(CURDIR)"`, `$(MAKE) -C "$(TEMP_DIR)/$*"`, etc.).
- Add contributor to `AUTHORS`.

### Testing
- Tested `make -n ARCH=x86-64-universal COMP=clang build` in a path containing spaces (`.../Stockfish Path With Spaces/src`). Before this patch it failed immediately during Makefile parsing; with this patch it parses cleanly with 0 warnings.
- Tested `make -j4 build ARCH=x86-64-universal COMP=clang` in a path containing spaces: successfully compiled and linked all slices.
- Tested `make build ARCH=apple-silicon COMP=clang` and ran `./stockfish bench 16 1 1`: all 51 positions evaluated identically.
- Tested `make universalclean` and `make clean`.

Fixes #7259

closes https://github.com/official-stockfish/Stockfish/pull/7260

No functional change
commits.subject: Makefile: fix universal build when source directory path contains spaces

Ensure valid score range for seekMate

With MultiPV, score is set to -VALUE_INFINITE on fail low.
These lines are then incorrectly searched with seekMate
starting at depth 3 (seekMate threshold 25194).
If score is just checked against -VALUE_INFINITE,

With this patch, we use previousScore for MultiPV to use the

In addition, it includes a patch by @HappyNoah-1 that only calculates

commits.author: xiangqishare <100093845+xiangqishare@users.noreply.github.com>
commits.message:
Unroll NNUE feature updates

Clang 23.1.4 leaves the fixed-size loops in `apply_feature_single()` and `apply_feature_pair()` rolled for `x86-64-avx512` and `x86-64-vnni512`. Since `Tile` is passed and returned by value, this causes repeated 1 KiB stack copies during feature updates, including with PGO.

Request full unrolling with `#pragma clang loop unroll(full)` for Clang and `#pragma GCC unroll(Tiling::NumRegs / 2)` for GCC, without an AVX512-specific guard. Clang needs its own spelling because Clang 11 does not recognize `#pragma GCC unroll`.

The initial Clang-only patch improved NPS by about 41% in a short local non-PGO test on Linux with a Xeon Platinum 8573C, Clang 23.1.4 (`7a941dfb2877`) and full LTO: three alternating before/after pairs, one pinned thread, 256 MiB hash, and four positions at 1M nodes each. No Fishtest run yet.

Compatibility checks, all with `-Werror`:

| Compiler | Targets and checks |
|---|---|
| GCC 9.3 | AVX2 and AVX512 accumulator compilation |
| Clang 11.1 | AVX2 full LTO build; SSE4.1, AVX2 and AVX512 accumulator compilation; AVX2 unoptimized debug accumulator |
| GCC 13.3 | AVX2 and AVX512 accumulator objects unchanged |
| Clang 20.1.2 | AVX2 and AVX512 accumulator objects unchanged |
| Clang 23.1.5 | SSE4.1, AVX2, AVX512 and VNNI512 accumulator objects unchanged; AVX512 full LTO binary unchanged |

“Unchanged” means byte-for-byte identical to the previous PR revision (`b63a546`). Both full builds retain bench `1559611` and identical scores, PVs and node counts across all 51 default positions at 20k nodes. These compatibility checks are not new speed measurements.

Prepared with assistance from OpenAI Codex.

closes https://github.com/official-stockfish/Stockfish/pull/7251

No functional change

Makefile: read only the major version for the gcc LTO partition check

GCC only prints a bare major number from `-dumpversion` when it was configured with `--with-gcc-major-version-only`, which the distro packages do. The official gcc docker images and toolchains built from source print the full version, so the gcc <= 13 guard from e5c99a892ed3 ends up running `test "13.5.0" -le 13`, which fails with "Illegal number" and quietly picks `-flto-partition=balanced` for exactly the compilers it was written to exclude. commits.author: Godsdar <ildar.popov.dev@gmail.com>
commits.message:
Scale the single-root-move time cap in nodestime mode

The single-root-move time cap is expressed in milliseconds, but `totalTime` and `elapsed()` use nodes when `nodestime` is enabled. The unscaled `500.0` therefore caps the allocation at 500 nodes regardless of the configured nodes per millisecond. Scale this cap by `limits.npmsec`, using 1 when nodestime is disabled.

This affects positions with one legal move and searches restricted to one root move with `searchmoves`. The existing 0.5-second policy is unchanged with the default `nodestime=0`.

To reproduce, send these commands interactively and wait for `bestmove`:

```text
setoption name nodestime value 1000
ucinewgame
isready
position fen 7k/8/8/8/8/r7/1N6/K7 w - - 0 1
go wtime 120000 btime 120000 nodes 2000000
```

Against master `effdc3fd3f6de6e75fe1374a51a7a7eed66f880b`, with one thread and the default network:

| nodestime | Master nodes / depth | Patched nodes / depth |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 666 / 8 | 666 / 8 |
| 10 | 666 / 8 | 13351 / 11 |
| 100 | 666 / 8 | 54330 / 14 |
| 1000 | 666 / 8 | 591911 / 28 |

The cap is checked between iterations, so these node counts can exceed the allocation. The same issue and correction were reproduced with Black to move and with `position startpos` plus `searchmoves e2e4`. Unrestricted start-position searches retained identical node counts, depths, and best moves at all four nodestime settings.

Validation: all 75 instrumented tests passed in both optimized and ASan+UBSan debug builds on Apple Silicon; the 16-case reproduction matrix also passed with sanitizers. Clang-format 20.1.8 and the signature test passed.

Default bench unchanged: **1559611**. No Fishtest run or playing-strength gain is claimed.

closes https://github.com/official-stockfish/Stockfish/pull/7238

No functional change
commits.subject: Scale the single-root-move time cap in nodestime mode

commits.author: Godsdar <ildar.popov.dev@gmail.com>
commits.message:
Reject oversized Syzygy symbol tables

`set_sizes()` reads the symbol count from the tablebase as a `u16`, but `btreeBuf`, `symlen` and `colour` have only `SymCount` (4096) entries. The existing `fits()` check bounds the source bytes, so a malformed table with a larger count can pass that check and overrun the destination in `memcpy()` and the subsequent symbol loop.

Reject counts greater than `SymCount` through the existing corrupt-table path before copying or iterating. Counts up to and including `SymCount` keep their existing handling. This applies to both WDL and DTZ loading.

Validation on macOS arm64 with Apple Clang:

- Optimized Apple silicon build; changed translation unit compiled with `-Werror`.
- All 75 upstream instrumented tests passed on a debug build with AddressSanitizer and UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer, including the Syzygy tests.
- Baseline and patched default benches both searched 1,559,611 nodes.
- `tests/signature.sh 1559611` and `git diff --check` passed.

The bounds error was identified and checked by source inspection; a malformed-tablebase runtime reproducer was not run. Windows and Linux validation remain for CI.

Prepared with OpenAI Codex, including source analysis and testing.

No functional change for valid tablebases.

closes https://github.com/official-stockfish/Stockfish/pull/7237

No functional change
commits.subject: Reject oversized Syzygy symbol tables

commits.author: ayushthepiro11-design <237785622+ayushthepiro11-design@users.noreply.github.com>
commits.message:
Pair int8 weight rows in accumulator updates

Since SFNNv18 every feature-transformer weight row (piece-square, threat and pawn-pair features) is stored as int8 and widened to int16 while it is added to or subtracted from the accumulator. On x86 the widening is done with one sign extension (vpmovsxbw) per vector register, and the accumulator update is bound by the shuffle port that executes it.

This patch widens two rows at once: the bytes of the two rows are interleaved with unpacklo/unpackhi_epi8 and each pair is summed by a maddubs against a vector of ones, which costs one shuffle per two rows instead of one per row. The weight rows are permuted at load time (FeatureTransformer::WideningPairOrder, inverted again by export_net) so that the accumulator layout stays unchanged. Rows of all feature sets with the same sign are collected (WeightRows) and processed together so that nearly every row has a partner; a leftover row is widened on its own with unpack + shift. Enabled for SSSE3 and better; other targets are unchanged.

Measured with an interleaved bench comparison (1 thread) on an Ice Lake server core:

  x86-64-avx512icl   +7.0% nps
  x86-64-avx2        +5.2% nps
  x86-64-sse41-popcnt +10.7% nps

Non-functional change: node counts are identical to master for the avx512icl, avx2, sse41-popcnt, sse2 and scalar builds, including debug and sanitized builds, and export_net reproduces the original net file.

commits.author: Carlos Esparza <ca2010es@gmail.com>
commits.message:
Only generate legal moves in movegen

The main changes here are by @rhirsch123. I have added some speedups and identified some more code that can be removed if we only ever deal with legal moves.
The only(?) important implementation detail of legal move generation is that we now keep a bitboard of squares threatened by `~sideToMove` in `Position`, to help with king move generation. For speed and conciseness, we include x-ray threats through the `sideToMove`-colored king (this only matters when `sideToMove` is in check). As a bonus, these bitboards get re-used in quiet move scoring.

Things that can be simplified once we have legal movegen:
- We can merge the `legal()` and `pseudo_legal()` methods
- Since we have threat bitboards, we no longer need `attackers_to_exist()` in `legal()`, so we can remove that method
- We don't need a separate `generate<LEGAL>` method that performs legality checks
- This also means the `NON_EVASIONS` movegen target becomes redundant

The change to `ray_pass_bb()` is outdated but should still be beneficial for performance.

commits.message:
Remove three always-true conditions in search

removes three conditions in search.cpp that can no longer be false:

step 6, Case B: this branch is only reached when the TT entry was deep enough but Case A did not apply. That means the bound is the opposite one-sided bound, so `ttData.bound != BOUND_EXACT` and the bound-direction check always hold. Only `depth > 5` needed

the branch before capture countermove bonus already handles `!priorCapture && prevSq != SQ_NONE`, so `priorCapture` is always true here.
qsearch stand pat: `bestValue` is either the clamped static eval or a TT value that already passed `!is_decisive`, so it can never be decisive at this point (since b0870cf5).
